statement: What is the size of one interior angle of a regular twelve-sided polygon?

choices.misconception: I found the exterior angle and answered with that instead of the interior one.
I used 360 divided by 12 subtracted from 195, or otherwise slipped a step in the arithmetic.
I gave the total of all twelve interior angles rather than one of them.
I used a ten-sided polygon by mistake.

hints: The exterior angles of any polygon always add to 360 degrees.
Each exterior angle of a regular 12-gon is 360 / 12 = 30 degrees.
Interior and exterior angles sit on a straight line, so the interior angle is 180 - 30 = 150 degrees.

solutions.reliable: The exterior angles of any convex polygon sum to 360 degrees, so in a regular twelve-sided figure each exterior angle is 360 / 12 = 30 degrees. An interior angle and its exterior angle lie on a straight line, so the interior angle is 180 - 30 = 150 degrees. Cross-check with the other formula: the interior angles total (12 - 2) x 180 = 1800 degrees, and 1800 / 12 = 150. The transferable idea: the exterior route is shorter and almost always safer.
solutions.elegant: Exterior angles share 360 degrees twelve ways, giving 30 each, so the interior angle is 150.

whyOnTest: Answering with the exterior angle, or with the total rather than one angle, are the two errors this question is built to catch.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
